title: 19 reported 'black triangle' UFO sightings across Leicestershire mapped

The sightings were reportedly made in the last five years

15:19, 31 Oct 2026

A total of 19 'black triangle' UFO sightings have been reported across Leicestershire in the last five years.

‌

‌

In total, nearly 2,000 Unidentified Flying Objects (UFOs) have been documented and logged in the UK over the last five years by the research group, UFO Identified.

‌

In Leicestershire, there have been 19 sightings in total, six of which were above the city centre. Outside of the city, two sightings were recorded in Ashby and another two in Market Harborough.

‌

A searchable interactive map allows you to explore every unexplained encounter logged in your area between 2021 and 2026. You can check what UFOs have been seen where you live using our interactive gadget.

The Pentagon recently published its latest release of declassified files on Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena (UAP – the American term for UFO), following an executive order signed by Donald Trump.

‌

Among the documents is an account from two federal agents stationed at a US “sensitive national security site” in June 2026.

According to the report, a matte-black triangular object with an estimated 15-foot wingspan hovered silently roughly 300 feet in the air for 20 seconds before descending into a canyon at high speed without leaving an exhaust trail.

‌

While orbs, spheres and “star-like” sightings make up the bulk of British sightings, researchers have logged 164 reports of similar wedge-shaped objects – meaning roughly one in every 12 sightings involves a distinctive triangle.

‌

The most recent sighting in the UK was on Wednesday, July 22, when a “large black triangle” featuring a red light on each point was witnessed hovering over Stretford in Greater Manchester for more than 30 minutes.

Earlier this year, a “perfect triangle” was seen speeding across the sky above Chesterfield in Derbyshire, a “black V-shaped boomerang” was spotted over the Fylde coast in Lancashire, and a soundless black wedge above Exmouth in Devon.

‌

The accounts have been gathered by UFO Identified to create a central, searchable public archive, called the UK UFO Database, to help researchers identify patterns.

Ash Ellis, founder of UFO Identified, said: "There are thousands of people across the UK who have seen something they could not readily explain, but the reports are often difficult to find once the initial interest has passed.

"We wanted to build a serious, easy-to-use public archive that keeps those accounts accessible and allows people to look for patterns for themselves."
